# S5 — the training progression, session by session

Written 2026-08-08. This is the **schedule and the stopping rules**, not the recipe (that is
`S5_RECIPE.md`). Its purpose is to make every session cost bounded and every decision made on our
own measurement rather than on a paper's.

---

## 0. The arithmetic every session is priced against

**Corrected.** I originally scoped capture at the prefill rate. That was wrong: the responses must be
**regenerated by the target**, which is a *generate* job at the suite-mean spec rate, and it is
**88 % of the wall time**.

```
prefill  62.4 tok/s   (F88)          prompt ~200 tok  ->  N x 200 / 62.4
generate 22.66 tok/s  (F96 suite)    response ~512 tok ->  N x 512 / 22.66
```

| samples | prefill | generate | total | days |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | 0.2 h | 1.3 h | **1.4 h** | 0.06 |
| **500** | 0.4 h | 3.1 h | **3.6 h** | 0.15 |
| 2 000 | 1.8 h | 12.6 h | **14.3 h** | 0.60 |
| 5 000 | 4.5 h | 31.4 h | **35.8 h** | 1.49 |
| 20 000 | 17.8 h | 125.5 h | **143.3 h** | 5.97 |

**Consequence for planning: B9's +30 % prefill work moves the SMALL term.** It was worth doing on its
own merits, and it does not meaningfully shrink capture. Anything that speeds up *generation* —
including the fine-tune itself — shrinks the next capture.

**Storage is never the constraint** at one epoch: capture a shard, train on it, delete it. Peak is
one shard, and a 2 K-sample shard is 49 GB bf16 against 122 GB free (F90).

---

## 1. The measurement protocol — fixed for every session

Changing how we measure between sessions would make the progression meaningless, so this is frozen:

- **8-prompt suite** from `scripts/prompt_suite.json`, one per category, ids from the checkpoint's
  own tokenizer, self-gated on `The capital of France is` -> `671,6102,294,8760,344`.
- **NGEN0 >= 200**, because F92 measured tau at **1.39 over the first 32 generated tokens** rising to
  ~3.2 only after ~128, as the drafter's 128-token sliding window fills. **A tau measured on a short
  generation is a transient, not a steady state.**
- **Block 6, adaptK 1.50** — the shipped default (F94/F96).
- **CLEAN runs**: no `DSV4_DPROF`/`KSWEEP`/`SPECPROF`/`MOEUNION`. Clocks pinned, caches dropped.
- **`LOSSLESS GATE` must pass.** A fine-tuned head that changes the emitted sequence is a failure
  regardless of tau.
- The canonical 6-token prompt is a **control only**. It is the worst case and it regresses at
  block 6; it must not be quoted as the headline.

**Baseline to beat (F96):** suite mean **tau 3.54 / 22.66 tok/s**, base AR 13.76.

---

## 2. Session 1 — the narrow proof. 500 samples, ~4 h, GO/NO-GO

**Not a capability lift. A test of one measured defect.**

F45 measured, on this engine: acceptance **3.00 -> 2.08** when real draft proposals are fed back,
because the shipped heads are trained against a `DSPARK_NOISE_TID` placeholder at positions
1..BLK-1, so real proposals are off-distribution. That is the HASS free-running mismatch, it is
**live in our head**, and it is repairable by training alone — no corpus-scale question involved.

| | |
|---|---|
| **domain** | `reasoning` only (tau 1.85 — one of the three collapsed categories) |
| **samples** | 500, prompts from Open-PerfectBlend's reasoning slice |
| **capture** | ~3.6 h (88 % of it regeneration) |
| **training** | 1 epoch, AdamW (0.9,0.95), LR 5e-5 cosine, warmup 0.05, the shipped 3-term loss |
| **evaluate** | the `reasoning` prompt only, plus the full suite to check nothing regressed |

**Why one domain:** it is the cheapest possible falsification. If training on 500 in-domain samples
cannot move the domain those samples came from, no corpus size will.

### Stopping rules

| outcome | reading | action |
|---|---|---|
| `reasoning` tau **>= 2.6** | the defect is real and repairable | **GO to session 2** |
| tau **2.1-2.6** | real but small | go, but re-price: the full run is worth ~half what the papers imply |
| tau **< 2.1** (within noise of 1.85) | training does not move this head | **STOP. Restore the base head and close S5.** |
| suite mean **drops** | overfitting to one domain | STOP; the corpus must be mixed from the start |
| `LOSSLESS GATE` fails | we perturbed something the verify depends on | STOP and diagnose before anything else |

**Cost of a NO-GO: ~half a day.** That is the entire point of this session.

---

## 3. Session 2 — the intermediate. 2 000 samples, ~14 h, measure the SLOPE

Only if session 1 says GO.

| | |
|---|---|
| **domains** | the three collapsed categories — `reasoning`, `code_gen`, `explanation` (tau 1.68-1.85) |
| **samples** | 2 000, mixed across the three |
| **capture** | ~14.3 h |
| **evaluate** | full 8-prompt suite |

**The output that matters is not the tau — it is the slope** between 500 and 2 000. Two points on an
acceptance-vs-corpus curve is what decides session 3's size, and it is the number no paper can give
us because it is architecture- and checkpoint-specific.

Also test here, since the data exists and it is free:

- **Train at block 8.** F94 measured that the head generalises **exactly one position past its
  trained width of 5** — tau rises 5->6 and *falls* 6->8. Training at 8 is the only way to find out
  whether that limit is the training width or the architecture. **If it moves, the ceiling goes from
  7 to 9 and this is worth more than the acceptance gain itself.**
- **HASS-style context alignment on steps 2-3** — train later positions on imperfect draft features
  rather than clean ones. Costs nothing extra in capture.

### Stopping rules

| slope 500 -> 2000 | action |
|---|---|
| **>= +0.4 tau** | steep; session 3 at 5 000 is justified |
| **+0.15 to +0.4** | flattening; session 3 at 2 000 more, then stop |
| **< +0.15** | **saturated. Ship what session 2 produced.** |

---

## 4. Session 3 — the Pareto point, sized from OUR slope

The literature cannot size this for us, and the two regimes it describes are far apart: EAGLE-1
reports "low sensitivity to training data" and saturates early, while EAGLE-3 reports a scaling law
with no saturation at ~8x the corpus. **Our head is block-trained with a Markov head — neither
regime is obviously ours.** Sessions 1 and 2 measure which.

**The Pareto criterion, stated before the data so it cannot be fitted after:**

> Stop when the marginal session buys **less than +0.1 tau per 12 hours of capture.**

At the measured 7.664 tok/s per unit tau (F96), +0.1 tau is +0.77 tok/s — about **+3 %**. Half a day
of capture for +3 % is the break-even; below that the same time is better spent elsewhere.

Expected landing zone, stated as a band with its confidence:

| acceptance | suite tok/s | vs today | confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.54 (today) | 22.66 | — | measured |
| 4.0 | 25.6 | +13 % | medium |
| 4.5 | 28.8 | +27 % | low |
| 5.0 | 32.0 | +41 % | very low — needs block > 6 to be usable at all |

**The last row is why session 2's block-8 test matters more than its tau.** At block 6 the ceiling is
7, so tau 5.0 is already 71 % of the maximum. Past that, acceptance work is pointless without a
wider block, and a wider block needs a head trained at that width.

---

## 5. What each session leaves behind regardless of outcome

Even a NO-GO session produces:

1. **The token-frequency distribution of the target's own outputs** — which is exactly the FR-Spec
   ranking the draft-vocabulary trim needs (F97). That lever is worth +3.0-3.5 % and is currently
   blocked *only* on not having this data.
2. A **regenerated corpus** that is reusable for every later session.
3. A **measured point on the acceptance-vs-corpus curve** for this architecture, which does not
   exist in the literature.

**So session 1 is not a bet.** Its data has value even if its answer is no.

---

## 6. Safety, unchanged across all sessions

- Base head backed up at `~/model-backups/dspark-mtp-base-0731REAP`, **sha256-verified byte-for-byte**
  against source. All 2977 `mtp.*` tensors are in shards 46-48 and those shards contain nothing else,
  so restore is a file copy.
- Fine-tuned heads load through `argv[4]`, the **separate-WeightStore override path**, which was
  identity-verified in F90 (same weights through the override reproduce the baseline exactly). The
  checkpoint directory is never written.
- Every session's headline number is a **clean run with the LOSSLESS gate passing**, or it is not
  quoted.

---

## 7. Automation: how a session actually runs, and what it is guaranteed to leave behind

One command runs a session end to end and chains to the next **only on GO**:

```bash
scripts/s5_session.sh s1 <prompts> 500 512  [next_name next_prompts next_n]
```

Seven steps, each verifying its own output before the next begins (`scripts/s5_session.sh`; the
three defects this design was written in response to are Finding 106):

| # | step | the check that must pass |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | pass 1 — regenerate with the target | every line starts with its **exact** seed prompt |
| 2 | pass 2 — capture taps, `lm_in`, engine probes | `read_capture.py` prints `VALIDATE: PASS` |
| 3 | equivalence gate, **before** training | port-vs-engine draft agreement >= 90 % |
| 4 | train | 1 epoch, warmup->cosine, `--metrics-out` |
| 5 | build a loadable head | fp8/E8M0 round-trip error <= 0.10 |
| 6 | eval on the frozen protocol | `LOSSLESS GATE ... PASS`, no instruments in the binary |
| 7 | archive, promote, decide | see below |

`S5_GEN=<file>` lets a session adopt a pass-1 dump produced outside the script. Pass 1 is the
expensive step; it is never redone blindly.

### Archive always, promote on merit, chain only on GO

These are **three different decisions** and the script keeps them separate:

* **Archive** is unconditional and happens *before* any judgement. Every head that training
  meaningfully produces is copied to `~/model-backups/heads/<name>/` with a sha256 per file, its
  `eval.log`, its `train_metrics.json` and a `head_card.json`, and gets a row in
  `HEAD_REGISTRY.md` — **including rejects**, so the record does not look like only winners
  existed. A rejected head is still a measured point on the acceptance-vs-corpus curve that
  session 3's size is chosen from; discarding it means re-paying its capture to learn the same
  thing twice.
* **Promote** (`tools/promote_head.py`) asks whether this head beats the incumbent across the whole
  suite by more than the 3.5 % run-to-run spread. It may fail without ending anything.
* **Chain** (`tools/session_gate.py`) applies §2's pre-registered rule. **This is deliberately not
  the promotion rule**: session 1 is a narrow single-domain proof and can legitimately say GO while
  failing a suite-wide bar. Gating the chain on promotion would discard exactly the evidence the
  session was built to produce. Exit 0 GO, 2 GO_REPRICE, 3 STOP; the chain continues on 0 and 2.

### Metrics captured per run

`train_metrics.json` — per-step loss/ce/tv/conf/grad_norm/lr history, plus the diagnostics that
distinguish a genuinely broad draft from a misaligned target: `draft-argmax == target-argmax`,
`== ground truth`, and the mean top-1 probability of each.

`session_verdict.json` — the verdict, the reasons, per-category tau and tok/s, base AR, and the
absolute path of the eval log it was derived from.

Both are archived with the head, so a number in `HEAD_REGISTRY.md` can always be traced back to the
run and the loss curve that produced it.
